scenario.goal: Follow a professional-services month from client receipts and cash sales to staff, rent, insurance and a corrected expense.
steps: Trace a monthly client receipt and separate cash activity in the bank and till accounts.
Review recurring staff, rent, utilities and insurance entries in the month-end journal.
Follow the year-end customer collection without recording income twice.
Review the mistaken cost, linked reversal and corrected replacement.
checks: Staff entries are illustrative support schedules, not payroll, withholding or employment compliance.
Client work is represented by general-ledger examples, not project management or time billing.
The open 2026 drafts are separate practice records and do not alter closed history.

anticipated_1_3.notice: Authored so the 1.3 features below have real history to act on the day they land. None of this is produced by a screen, a register or a scheduler in 1.2.0; every figure here was posted by an ordinary journal in the history above.

asset_register.convention: A full month in the month an asset enters service, and none in the month it is disposed of

loan_schedule.note: Two instalments are posted in the history. The remaining three are schedule data only; nothing generates them today.

year_end.note: The 2025 periods are closed, which blocks backdated posting. No closing journal has been posted and no year is locked: 1.2.0 has neither, and the balances above are what a year-end close would have to work from.

period_close.note: There is no reverse-on flag and no cash-count document in 1.2.0; these name the history a close checklist would ask about.

learning_story.origin: Mira and Noel opened a two-person design studio above a former print shop. Mira looks after client projects; Noel keeps the monthly records. They want stable retainers without confusing deposits, earned fees and cash.
learning_story.notice: Fictional background is storytelling. Only linked recorded events change the sample books. Amounts are illustrative base-currency units; no country tax rules are implied.

chapters.decision: Keep partner capital separate, move an actual float from bank to petty cash, and spread the insurance cost over its coverage period.
chapters.accounting: Owner funding is equity, the bank-to-cash transfer earns no income, and insurance starts as a prepayment.
chapters.inspect: Follow the recorded sources, then compare this month's profit and loss with the month-end trial balance.
